messages:
Ian (support): forwarding a customer report — ACME saw trial credits not decrementing after a burst of quick requests. customer says tokens in dashboard didn’t change but API returned 200 for generations. pasted their request logs below.

Ian (support): customer provided these request ids: r_20260301_01, r_20260301_02, r_20260301_03. they also show idempotency-key reused across retries: IK-ACME-42 in all three.

Ian (support): their short repro: start a streaming chat request, get a 200 stream, then client cancels and retries with same idempotency key. they claim credits remain unchanged.

Meera (devex): assigning, can you paste the raw request/response (headers + small body) they sent? also need org id and the session id if available.

Ian (support): pasted sanitized headers from the customer: 
```
POST /v1/chat/stream
Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED
X-Idempotency-Key: IK-ACME-42
Content-Type: application/json
Body: {"model":"redwood-500m","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summarize"}],"stream":true}
```

Ian (support): customer log of sequence: first request returned 200, then client socket closed after partial stream, they retried immediately with same idempotency key, got 200 again. dashboard credits stayed the same.

Dan (sre): quick check of ledger for those request ids — no debit rows for r_20260301_01/02/03. I do see ledger entries with state=\"hold\" and reason=\"checkout_hold\" created at 2026-03-01T12:34:56Z for that org. looks like finalize step never arrived. billing-bot posted an event: 

billing-bot: EVENT ledger_hold_created org=org_acme hold_id=HLD-9999 amount=0.00 state=hold reason=checkout_hold

Dan (sre): the interesting bit — hold amount is 0.00 because the session was short and we deferred pricing calc to finalize. finalize webhook to our billing pipeline shows a 502 around the same time, likely from the worker that computes token counts under high parallelism.

Maya (billing): if finalize never ran, credits won't move from pending -> consumed. customer-facing dashboard shows total credits (available + pending) which confused them. we should surface pending holds in UI but fix server flow.

Meera (devex): possible root cause candidate: idempotency-key reuse across aborted streaming connections suppresses a finalize call path. repro plan:
1) send streamed request with X-Idempotency-Key header
2) close client mid-stream (simulate user cancel)
3) retry immediately reusing the same idempotency key and observe which code path the runtime takes for finalization

Meera (devex): quick curl repro (non-streaming to simulate lifecycle):
```
# initial request (simulate partial then cancel)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" -H "X-Idempotency-Key: IK-ACME-42" -d '{"model":"redwood-500m","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"x"}],"stream":true}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
# kill the connection after 1s (ctrl-c) then immediately:
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" -H "X-Idempotency-Key: IK-ACME-42" -d '{"model":"redwood-500m","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"x"}],"stream":true}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
```

Dan (sre): I’ll tail the finalize-worker logs and add extra logging for idempotency handling and finalize webhook retries. suspect race where first aborted session creates hold but never queues finalize because the retry short-circuits to an existing in-progress session state.

Maya (billing): mitigation — schedule a backfill job to finalize any holds older than 5s for affected orgs, and credit the customer immediately if we confirm no debit applied. we can do a one-off credit-adjustment for ACME while fix is rolled out.

Ian (support): I told the customer we’ll run the backfill and issue a corrective adjustment if we confirm tokens weren't consumed. they asked for ETA.

Dan (sre): ETA: I’ll add logging now and run backfill in 30–60m, then post results here.

Meera (devex): will add a short doc with repro steps and a small sample script they can run to reproduce safely in a sandbox.

Maya (billing): once backfill completes I’ll post the ledger rows and the adjustment id.

Ian (support): thanks team — I’ll update the customer after the backfill completes. :thumbsup:
